Subject: Post-demo: SDK onboarding + throttling & idempotency plan

Hi Tina / Michael —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + what I propose as next steps so we can get a small integration POC going: 

Recap (what we showed)
- SDK quickstart (client init, streaming, structured output/tool-calls)
- Embeddings + reranker flow for semantic search (precompute vectors, real-time rerank calls)
- Routing/fallback: hosted model -> pinned dedicated variant for heavy traffic -> local/private for regulated flows
- Observability: per-token cost + latency dashboards, request tracing

Main asks we captured from your team
- Confirm expected steady-state QPS and peak TPS for inference and embedding ingestion
- Clarify whether you need Dedicated capacity (SLA) vs Hosted with burst allowance
- Security/compliance artifacts (SOC 2 evidence, data retention controls)

Recommended tactical plan (next 2 weeks)
1) Tech call with your infra + our SE (Marissa) to walk SDK auth, routing, and embedding lifecycle (45m)
2) Provide a sandbox API key + a pre-populated sample index for reranking tests
3) Run a small ingest test (5k docs) and sample rerank latency profile; capture 429s and tune batch size
4) Iterate on retry/backoff and idempotency approach (we recommend request IDs + exponential backoff with jitter)

Initial notes on throttling & idempotency (high level)
- Rate limits are enforced per-customer and per-route; short bursts can be accommodated via token bucket bursting but sustained throughput needs Dedicated capacity
- When you see 429s: use exponential backoff (base 100ms -> 200ms -> 400ms) with full jitter and max cap (we typically cap at ~5s for user-facing flows)
- For idempotency: attach a stable client-generated ID header (X-Request-ID) on requests that mutate state or represent a single intent; server returns 409/200 with referenced result for duplicate IDs
- For embedding ingests, we recommend batching at encoder side (e.g., 128 vectors) and using per-batch ids for dedupe on retry

Attachments: acme_redwood_arch_sketch.pdf (architecture sketch), sdk_quickstart_snippet.txt (example init + auth), acme_compliance_request.xlsx (your questionnaire)

Open items we need from you:
- Target TPS (p95) for text generation and for reranker calls
- Security contact to exchange SOC 2 artifact zip or arrange an NDA for on-prem artifacts

Can we schedule the 45m tech call tomorrow (Thu) at 10am PT? Marissa and Aditya will join to cover SDK + routing details.

Thanks —

Hi Tina / Michael —

Quick technical follow-up from my side ahead of the call. I captured recommended defaults and a minimal SDK snippet to get you started. I'll walk through these on the call.

1) Auth + tokens- we support API keys (long-lived) and short-lived session tokens (recommended for client-side). For infra: API keys rotated via KMS, and we can issue scoped short-lived tokens (1h) tied to an account id for sandbox.

2) SDK init (pseudo)
- client = RedwoodClient(api_key=process.env.RW_KEY, region='us-west')
- client.configure({retry: 'custom', maxAttempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 100})

3) Routing & fallbacks- For your burst profile we recommend hosted + burst allowance for initial POC. If steady-state > 100qps sustained, move to Dedicated to guarantee latency. Use routing policy: prefer "pinned-dedicated" when available, otherwise fall back to high-performance hosted model. Implement client-side hinting header X-Preferred-Model: dedicated-v1

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern- Ingest pipeline: precompute vectors in bulk (batch size 64–128) into your index. For query time: compute query embedding + call reranker endpoint with top-k candidates (k=50). Server-side scoring is shallow and fast; common p95s are ~120–300ms depending on model and seq-length. Tune batch size before increasing retry attempts.

5) 429 handling & idempotency (detailed)
- 429s are a signal of token-bucket exhaustion for the route. Client policy: exponential backoff with full jitter (J. B. Salvatore pattern). Suggested algorithm: attempt = 0; while attempt < maxAttempts: delay = min(maxCap, base * 2**attempt); sleep(random_uniform(0, delay)); attempt++
- Base values we use for interactive flows: base=100ms, maxCap=5000ms, maxAttempts=6
- Idempotency: add header X-Request-ID (UUID v4) for user-intent calls and batch ingestion. Server will dedupe within a window (48h). On duplicate, server returns 200 with existing result or 409 for conflicting mutates.
- Retry semantics: safe retries for non-mutating calls (generation, retrieval). For mutating operations, use idempotency keys and wait for explicit success/duplicate indicators.

6) Practical ops tips
- For embedding ingests, prefer larger batches to reduce per-vector cost and reduce 429s. But keep batch size balanced against memory/latency.
- Use our SDK's built-in circuit-breaker hook to automatically throttle client-side when p95 latency spikes.

Attachments included: sdk_quickstart_snippet.txt (init + alt) and a slightly updated architecture sketch acme_redwood_arch_sketch.pdf. I've also added a link to our onboarding doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/onboarding

Next: Priyom, Aditya — can you provision a sandbox API key scoped to the ACME account and drop it into a sealed S3 link before the call? I can demo the ingest flow using their sample dataset.

–Marissa
